Zero-Coupon Bond Prices from DNS Factors

Source: R/dns-pricing.R
dns_zero_prices.Rd

Prices zero-coupon bonds off a DNS curve.

Usage

dns_zero_prices(factors, maturities, lambda = ns_lambda(3.5), face = 100)

Arguments

factors

Array or matrix. DNS factors, as in dns_discount_factors.

maturities

Numeric vector. Maturities in years.

lambda

Numeric. DNS decay parameter lambda, per unit of maturity. Maturities here are in years, and the default places the curvature hump at 3.5 years, near the middle of a Treasury curve. It is written as ns_lambda(3.5) so the number states its own meaning; see ns_lambda. Diebold and Li's 0.0609 is a month-denominated constant and in years would place that hump at 29.4 years.

face

Numeric. Face value of the bond. Defaults to 100.

Value

Prices in the same shape as dns_discount_factors.

Details

A zero-coupon bond is worth its face value discounted to today, so this is face times the discount factor. It is separated out because quoting per 100 of face is the market convention.

See also

dns_discount_factors, dns_par_yields

Examples

data(treasury_yields)
maturities <- as.numeric(setdiff(names(treasury_yields), "Date"))
curve <- fit_ns_model(maturities, as.numeric(treasury_yields[nrow(treasury_yields), -1]))
factors <- matrix(curve$parameters[1:3], nrow = 1)

round(dns_zero_prices(factors, maturities, curve$parameters[["lambda"]])[1, ], 3)
#>  [1] 99.635 98.921 97.882 95.872 91.951 88.043 80.307 72.955 62.997 38.497
#> [11] 23.519
